sections.value:
**Verdict: block** at `a552625169d54b45015c6681b689da334b470987` (F161), under C33/C34.

Scoped identity rendering and command quoting hold. The promised 2 KB cap is broken by ordinary requests across distinct holding addresses. PM confirmed this is the same normal-use cost-cap defect as performance finding P208-F001 and requires repair, not a C34 follow-up.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs | 1826-1892 | Normal-use correctness/cost: uncapped release-command footer and unconditional first line can exceed the 2 KB notice limit | 9/10 |

## Cap failure

For grouped notices, every distinct request address contributes a release command to `releases`. `notice_next` joins all those commands into the footer without bounding them.

The line loop reserves space for that footer, but stops only when `shown > 0`, so it unconditionally appends the first request line. It finally appends the entire footer. If ordinary requests for many roles/instances generate a footer larger than the available budget, withholding later request lines cannot make the final message fit.

The 60-request regression uses one address and therefore deduplicates to one release command. It does not cover the normal many-addresses case. Cap the complete rendered message, including footer and first line, and exercise distinct addresses; preserve an accurate omission count.

This is not a hostile same-user request or an optional hardening demand. It violates the stated normal-use output/cost bound. PM said the round-two repair is already being prepared.

## Rendering and admission disposition

Seat/request/instance rendering remains closed; role/project admission supplies their normal grammars. Printed revive/release commands quote complete arguments. Revive text is guidance, not an executed command or new authority.

The cap keeps complete strings, so it does not split UTF-8 characters. Character safety alone does not establish the total byte bound.

The grouped message uses its oldest member's id. Unadmitted members release their claims for retry; admitted groups stamp every included member, including those omitted from the displayed list. At-least-once recovery remains disclosed.

Do not interpret “at most one extra message per group” as a proven bound under repeated partial stamp failures: members are stamped separately and recovered under their own ids. No additional blocking failure was established from that qualification here.

## CI and scope

Local/remote/GitHub heads agree; detached shared worktree clean; the sole scoped commit is the reviewed head.

CI [42573708131](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42573708131) succeeded on merge `2f6bfc2c41b53ed0c30b5582bcbdaf9ed231664c`, with this head and main `f7744c5c3f677732af8b3c0a4dad657544811ce0` as parents. Tree `705284167a3cd8db3a9e2fcd566b1bf5dfbbad4e` matches the reviewed head.

JUnit artifact [13654273061](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42573708131/artifacts/13654273061) confirms 2,341 passing cases, no failures; six separately skipped. Three-request gone-holder grouping/all stamps/next-round quiet, the 60-request single-address cap case and the updated singleton gone-holder case executed successfully.

No local builds/tests, mutants, credential reads, live-system probes or product edits. C33 same-user isolation is not a finding; C34 optional fixtures/inventories are not gates. This block is the specifically confirmed normal-use cap bug, not a new general security requirement.
